experiment: Real isolated local engine containers; not AWS conformance or repository tests

decision.reason: No unmodified tested candidate meets acknowledged-write crash durability plus current Kinesis record-size/API boundaries. kinesis-mock loses acknowledged records after immediate process kill. Kinesalite retains process-crash writes but hard-rejects data above1MiB, lacks consumers/event streams and cannot relinquish wall-clock retention. Do not conceal these gaps with a receipt/redo ledger.

transport.baseline: scripts/aws/aws_cli.py run/result for signed create-stream on explicit localhost endpoint
transport.remaining_calls: Python stdlib HTTP AWS JSON1.1 with synthetic Authorization scope; backend routing does not validate cryptographic signature; no production credentials loaded
transport.event_stream: Actual first SubscribeToShard frame read; prelude and full message CRC32 verified
transport.compaction: Data replaced by decoded length/SHA256; opaque iterator values replaced by length/SHA256; sequence numbers and timestamps retained. Empty response JSON decode errors on initial mock CreateStream/SplitShard are capture-parser observations, HTTP200 empty body is the actual result. Parser corrected before later calls.

boundaries: README advertises0.4.8; latest release endpoint returned0.6.2 published2026-05-29.
Create/Put/Get, PutRecords, split/merge and closed parent reads succeed. Closed shards return child shards and null next iterator at exhaustion.
Different signing region and12-digit account route to distinct streams. This is namespace selection, not authentication proof.
Consumer registration becomesACTIVE and SubscribeToShard returns real application/vnd.amazon.eventstream frame containing stored records with valid CRCs.

Default data limit1048576 bytes; UpdateMaxRecordSize10240KiB permits2MiB and10MiB writes. A10MiB record with3-byte partition key then yields GetRecords HTTP500, engine log: java.util.NoSuchElementException: last on empty queue.
Periodic full JSON snapshots from in-memory Ref; disk write not part of acknowledged PutRecord. Graceful stop retained write, immediate SIGKILL lost write.
Utils.now uses IO.realTime. Arrival-time request extension ignored. Iterator expired after304.834wall seconds including restarts. No environment/config/public API clock injection.
Retention API24..8760h; GetRecords never filters record age in tagged source. ListShards filters closed shard age against wall time. No disable-retention knob; day-scale expiry was not awaited.

Control-operation limits are fixed concurrent semaphores, released on operation completion, not per-second token refill. No PutRecord/PutRecords/GetRecords per-shard wall-clock rate enforcement found in tagged source; no disabling knob required for an absent limiter.

boundaries: Create/Put/Get, PutRecords, split/merge and closed-shard reads work against actual LevelDB.
Immediate process SIGKILL retains acknowledged write. leveldown writes default sync:false; host failure/fsync durability NOT established. Meta and data puts are separate, not one atomic batch.

CLI ignores SIGTERM as PID1, docker stop needed forcedSIGKILL after15s; SIGINT exits1. A lifecycle-only launcher using documented programmatic server and public server.close closed LevelDB cleanly with exit0 and successful same-volume reopen.
Account/region headers ignored; scope is per-process AWS_ACCOUNT_ID/AWS_REGION environment.
Hard1MiB data validator,7MiB request-body ceiling; UpdateMaxRecordSize/consumer APIs/SubscribeToShard return UnknownOperationException.
Date.now owns arrival timestamps, iterator expiry300s and record retention. No service-clock injection in exported options. Supplied arrival timestamp ignored.
GetRecords filters and asynchronously deletes expired rows. HTTP retention max168h;8760 rejected by validator. No disable knob. Day-scale expiry not awaited.
No per-second request/shard rate enforcement found in source; shardLimit is a count cap, not rate.

primary_sources.purpose: Actual current version and multi-account release
Periodic snapshot write, not ack durability
No age filter and empty queue defect
Public close and real store shutdown
sync defaults false; no host-power-loss guarantee

limitations: JVM kinesis-mock executable not executed; it shares same persistence/API Scala source.
No host-power-cut experiment, native AWS calls, full24h expiry wait, or throughput benchmark.
Single immediate crash trial per candidate; results establish observed loss/survival, not a quantified reliability rate.
No patched engine, alternate backend implementation, replay log or service-time shim invented.

command_note: Command inventory, not chronological shell replay. All service run/start --attach commands were launched through hub supervision and passed readiness via localhost port. Reopen/crash phases repeated at the observed timestamps. Crash kill_delay_seconds measures docker kill command duration; HTTP200 was followed by local evidence serialization then that kill, without intentional sleep.
